cell.label: Dementia suspected: perform history (timing, risk factors, family history, head trauma, education) and interview caregiver. Perform physical exam (signs of previous stroke, hyperreflexia, Babinski signs, gait apraxia, pseudobulbar palsy).
Administer brief cognitive test (e.g., Mini-Mental State Examination,Time and Change). Do history, physical, and cognitive test suggest dementia?
Lab evaluation: CBC, TSH, electrolytes, serum calcium, fasting glucose, B12. Abnormal?

Age <60, rapid decline over 1-2 months, duration of dementia <2 years, recent head trauma, unexplained neurologic symptoms, history of cancer, use of anticoagulants or bleeding disorder, history of urinary incontinence and gait disorder, new localizing signs, atypical presentation, or new gait disorder?

Alzheimer's dementia likely. Consider Lewy body dementia if prominent visual hallucinations and parkinsonian signs. Consider CJD and CSF 14-2-2 antigen testing if rapid decline with risk factors for CJD.
Evaluate and treat abnormal findings. Symptoms resolve?
Evaluate/treat the depression, source of delirium. Symptoms resolve?
